guide_line: Count electron groups on one atom, then name the hybrid.
steps: An electron group is one bond or one lone pair on the atom you were asked about. A double bond is one group. A triple bond is one group.
Count those groups. The number of hybrid orbitals equals that count.
Two groups use sp hybrids, and the angle is about 180°. Three groups use sp2, about 120°. Four groups use sp3, about 109.5°.
Five groups use sp3d. Six groups use sp3d2.

worked_example.q: What hybridization does C use in CH4?
steps: Carbon has four single bonds and no lone pair.

similar_problem.q: What hybridization does C use in CO2?
similar_problem.hint: Each double bond is one group, not two.

problems.q: What hybridization does C use in CH4?
problems.why: Carbon in CH4 has four single bonds and no lone pair. Four groups use sp3 hybrids.
hints: Carbon in CH4 has four single bonds and no lone pair.
Those four groups on carbon use sp3 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does C use in CO2?
problems.why: CO2 is O=C=O. Each double bond is one group, so carbon has two groups. Two groups use sp hybrids.
hints: Each C=O in CO2 is one group, so carbon has two groups.
Two groups on the carbon of CO2 use sp hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does C use in CH2O?
problems.why: Carbon in CH2O has two C–H bonds and one C=O double bond. That is three groups, so the hybrids are sp2.
hints: CH2O’s carbon has two C–H bonds plus one C=O, three groups.
Three groups on the carbon of CH2O use sp2 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does N use in NH3?
problems.why: Nitrogen has three N–H bonds and one lone pair. Four groups use sp3 hybrids.
hints: Nitrogen in NH3 has three bonds and one lone pair.
Three bonds plus that lone pair on nitrogen use sp3 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does O use in H2O?
problems.why: Oxygen has two O–H bonds and two lone pairs. Four groups use sp3 hybrids.
hints: Oxygen in water has two bonds and two lone pairs.
Two bonds plus two lone pairs on oxygen use sp3 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does B use in BF3?
problems.why: Boron has three B–F bonds and no lone pair. Three groups use sp2 hybrids.
hints: Boron in BF3 has three bonds and no lone pair.
Three groups on boron in BF3 use sp2 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does C use in HCN?
problems.why: HCN is H–C≡N. Carbon has two groups: the C–H bond and the triple bond. Two groups use sp hybrids.
hints: The C≡N in HCN is one group, plus the C–H bond.
Two groups on carbon in HCN use sp hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does P use in PCl5?
problems.why: Phosphorus has five P–Cl bonds and no lone pair. Five groups use sp3d hybrids.
hints: Phosphorus in PCl5 has five bonds and no lone pair.
Five groups on phosphorus use sp3d hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does S use in SF6?
problems.why: Sulfur has six S–F bonds and no lone pair. Six groups use sp3d2 hybrids.
hints: Sulfur in SF6 has six bonds and no lone pair.
Six groups on sulfur use sp3d2 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does Xe use in XeF4?
problems.why: Xenon has four Xe–F bonds and two lone pairs. Six groups use sp3d2 hybrids.
hints: XeF4 has four bonds and two lone pairs on xenon.
Six groups on xenon in XeF4 use sp3d2 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does each C use in C2H4?
problems.why: Each carbon in H2C=CH2 has two C–H bonds and one double bond. Three groups use sp2 hybrids.
hints: Each carbon in C2H4 has two C–H bonds and one C=C.
Three groups on each carbon of C2H4 use sp2 hybrids.

problems.q: What hybridization does each C use in C2H2?
problems.why: Each carbon in H–C≡C–H has one C–H bond and one triple bond. Two groups use sp hybrids.
hints: Each carbon in C2H2 has one C–H bond and one C≡C.
Two groups on each carbon of C2H2 use sp hybrids.
